title: Capacity qualification blueprint for enterprise dedicated requests — SLO decomposition, GPU-family guidance & burst policies
creator: Anika Rao
description:
This ticket defines a lightweight qualification rubric and decision blueprint for enterprise dedicated-capacity requests. It translates customer SLAs (latency SLOs, p95/p99, availability targets) and workload fingerprints (avg/peak RPS, token length distribution, ephemeral vs steady-state) into concrete reserved throughput commitments, GPU-family recommendations, and scaling policy templates. The goal is to: 1) reduce back-and-forth during sales/onboarding, 2) standardize sane defaults for reserve vs burst allocations, and 3) provide an explainable reasoning trail for pricing and SLA offers.

Key outcomes:
- A scoring rubric that maps SLA/traffic inputs to recommended GPU classes (T4/A10/A100/H100) and quantization suggestions
- Reserved throughput bands (low/medium/high) with burst buffer sizing and preemption tolerance guidance
- Scaling policy templates (autoscale thresholds, warm-up rules, cold-start mitigation, canary fallback) and contractual fallbacks
- Acceptance criteria: <5% manual escalations for qualifying small/medium accounts; handbook and onboarding checklist published; a follow-up ENG ticket to implement the recommendation API

Acceptance criteria (measurable):
- Pilot with 3 enterprise requests using the rubric before 2026-03-20
- Reduction in average intake turnaround from 6 business days to 72 hours for standard profiles
- Documentation and decision matrix published in Confluence + onboarding form in Drive
updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff with Sales Engineering and Solutions — captured common ask patterns (low-latency chat, document embeddings, high-volume batch embeddings).
2026-02-18: Drafted initial scoring rubric mapping p99 latency and tokens/sec to GPU families; Marcus Li suggested adding quantization tolerance bands and preemption sensitivity.
2026-02-25: Reviewed with Runtime team — agreed to include warm KV-cache sizing and prefix-caching recommendations for conversational workloads.
2026-03-01: Design reviewed UX for intake form; Sophie Nguyen requested a separate 'regulatory' flag for VPC/on-prem customers to surface private deployment constraints.
2026-03-03: Legal raised contract fallback language; added a contract clause template for degraded throughput fallback and dedicated-burst credits.
2026-03-05: Pilot intake 1 completed (large fintech customer) — recommendation: 4xA100 reserved + 20% burst buffer; preliminary feedback positive; next: instrument cost estimator in intake form.
